name: Community — MiniMax H3 (Heptagram Turbo)
author: eatyet
description: MiniMax H3 on eatyet's Heptagram Turbo v1.0: by the author's description a merge of several community H3 checkpoints with LoRA fine-tuning and the TaoMate and HyperFlow speed LoRAs built in. One 21.0 GB file from Civitai, no Turbo LoRA. Runs at the author's settings: res_multistep / simple, 8 steps, sigma shift 12 video / 3 audio (his ranges are 4 to 8 steps and shift 6 to 16). The author says it suits game, anime and 3D styles, and that matches what we saw: asked for felt stop-motion, it drifted to a smooth 3D-animated look on two of three prompt versions. Pick it when you want that look, and pick another card for handmade or photographic texture. The author also notes that this version's audio has flaws. Text to video only in this first release.

presets.name: MiniMax H3 Text to Video (Heptagram Turbo)
presets.description:
eatyet's Heptagram Turbo v1.0 (21.0 GB) on the plain official graph at the author's settings: res_multistep / simple, 8 steps, sigma shift 12 video / 3 audio. His stated ranges are 4 to 8 steps and shift 6 to 16; the Steps control covers 4 to 8. The speed LoRAs are part of the checkpoint, so there is no LoRA node and no second file.

This one has a look. The author says it works well for game, anime and 3D styles. In a one-seed comparison against eight other H3 checkpoints (2026-10-09, RTX 4070 Ti 12 GB, 864x480, 15 s, engine v0.38.0) on a prompt that asked for needle-felt stop-motion and excluded 3D CGI, it gave a smooth 3D-animated character with bright glints on the glass on two of three prompt versions. A structured three-shot brief pulled it back to a felt look and cut at the scripted 5 and 10 second marks. Choose it for stylised 3D animation, not for handmade or photographic texture. One seed and one scene, so treat this as a first impression.

The author notes that the audio in this version has some flaws; we did not judge the audio by ear.

About 5 1/2 minutes per 15-second clip at 480p. Free system RAM matters more than VRAM; keep 16 GB+ free.

Verified in SimpliGen 1.71.1 / engine v0.38.0 on a 12 GB RTX 4070 Ti: 15 s at 864x480, 8 steps, 338 s through the app, and the output matched the engine test frame for frame (same seed).
presets.tagline: Heptagram Turbo: 8 steps, leans to a 3D-animated look

requirements.notes: One 21.0 GB checkpoint from Civitai (the download worked without an API key on 2026-10-09). Eight steps by default, res_multistep/simple, sigma shift 12.0 video / 3.0 audio set in the workflow, inside the author's ranges (4-8 steps, shift 6-16). The author says the TaoMate and HyperFlow speed LoRAs are merged in, so there is no Turbo LoRA. Image and reference cards were added in 1.1.0 (2026-10-15). MEASURED 2026-10-09 (RTX 4070 Ti 12 GB, 31 GB RAM, 864x480, 15 s, engine 0.38.0, Faster Attention on, this card's graph submitted to the engine): 322-329 s per clip at 8 steps. Tested at eight steps only. IN-APP 2026-10-09 (SimpliGen 1.71.1): the same prompt and seed through this card took 338 s and produced video and audio identical to the engine test.

video.description: Animate a source image with Heptagram Turbo. The image becomes the first frame and the prompt describes the motion. Runs on the same checkpoint as this pack's text-to-video card, so there is no extra download. Your first and last frame images are CENTRE-CROPPED to the output shape, not letterboxed: match the aspect ratio to your picture, or a tall portrait at 16:9 loses the head.

video.description: Keep a person's appearance in a brand new shot with Heptagram Turbo. Supply one to three reference pictures of the SAME person; the reference never appears in the video, so the prompt must describe the whole shot (setting, action and camera), not just the movement.
